title: Rendering `*.qmd` vignette files
description:
Hello,

Does `pagedown` support rendering `*.qmd` vignette files? I saved the following simple script in the `vignettes/AA.qmd`.

```
---
title: "TITLE"
output: html_document
author: "AUTHOR"
date: "2025-02-19"
date-modified: "`r format(Sys.time(), '%d %B, %Y')`"
editor_options: 
  chunk_output_type: console
editor: 
  markdown: 
    wrap: 72
execute: 
  eval: false
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    code-overflow: wrap
    page-layout: full
    toc: true
    toc-title: "TOC_TITLE"
    toc-expand: true
    toc-depth: 2
    number-sections: true
    link-external-icon: true
    link-external-newwindow: true
---

# Level1
SOME TEXT

## Level2
SOME TEXT

### Level3
SOME TEXT
```

I get the following error when using `pkgdown::build_articles()` (although the same script works as expected when clicking on the knit button of RStudio):

```
── Building articles ──────────────────────────────────────────────
Writing articles/index.html
Reading vignettes/AA.qmd
Running `quarto render`

! System command 'quarto.exe' failed
Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see where the error occurred.

By renaming the same file from `vignettes/AA.qmd` to `vignettes/AA.Rmd`,  `pkgdown::build_articles()` works as expected, although with some options not considered in the resulted HTML; e.g.

For example, using the sample CV from the package, if I place the (large-ish) aside chunk after the `Teaching` heading or at the end of that section, the final position is the same

title: Markdow inserted figure are not listed in LOF
description:
This was found by @adamvi in https://github.com/rstudio/pagedown/pull/281#issuecomment-1074004390 It seems our LOF feature does not support markdown inserted figure like ````markdown ![(#fig:test) Test](https://cran.r-project.org/Rlogo.svg) ```` LOF is supposed to be build in our lua filter but we only process div of class figure https://github.com/rstudio/pagedown/blob/20dbdb1d32eeb4aaeccd1bb68e5a04917fb1764c/inst/resources/lua/loft.lua#L78-L88 and we proceed explicit block written in Raw HTML as we check also https://github.com/rstudio/pagedown/blob/20dbdb1d32eeb4aaeccd1bb68e5a04917fb1764c/inst/resources/lua/loft.lua#L56 So LOF works well when figure are included using **knitr** because `knitr::include_graphics()` will write the HTML directly this way ````html

(\#fig:unnamed-chunk-2)A caption.

```` as `native_divs` extensions is included in Pandoc conversion, a Div will be produced in the Native representation. But for markdown syntax, it won't be the case. I don't think this limitation is documented anywhere. In order to support this, here is the situation. This is what is produced for default markdown which is supposed to produce figures (`implicit_figures` extensions) ```` ❯ echo '![(#fig:test) Test](https://cran.r-project.org/Rlogo.svg)' | pandoc -t native -f markdown [ Para [ Image ( "" , [] , [] ) [ Str "(#fig:test)" , Space , Str "Test" ] ( "https://cran.r-project.org/Rlogo.svg" , "fig:" ) ] ] ```` This is when `-implicit_figures` is set to deactivate ````markdown ❯ echo '![(#fig:test) Test](https://cran.r-project.org/Rlogo.svg)' | pandoc -t native -f markdown-implicit_figures [ Para [ Image ( "" , [] , [] ) [ Str "(#fig:test)" , Space , Str "Test" ] ( "https://cran.r-project.org/Rlogo.svg" , "" ) ] ] ```` So AST is quite the same, except for the `fig:` appended to the title part of the Image ````markdown ❯ echo '![(#fig:test) Test](https://cran.r-project.org/Rlogo.svg "Title of the Graph")' | pandoc -t native -f markdown [ Para [ Image ( "" , [] , [] ) [ Str "(#fig:test)" , Space , Str "Test" ] ( "https://cran.r-project.org/Rlogo.svg" , "fig:Title of the Graph" ) ] ] ```` We should be able to account for this to make the LOF works. Also, in near future, there should be a Figure representation in Pandoc AST. That would help.

title: Adapt to Pandoc 2.17 changes
description:
There was a big change in Lua for Pandoc regarding how meta values are treated.
https://pandoc.org/releases.html#pandoc-2.17-2022-01-12

> Elements of type MetaValue are no longer pushed as values which have .t and .tag properties. This was already true for MetaString and MetaBool values, which are still marshaled as Lua strings and booleans, respectively. Affected values:
>
>    MetaBlocks values are marshaled as a Blocks list;
>    MetaInlines values are marshaled as a Inlines list;
>    MetaList values are marshaled as a generic pandoc Lists.
>    MetaMap values are marshaled as plain tables and no longer given any metatable.

We probably need to adjust some of our filters like
https://github.com/rstudio/pagedown/blob/7ed2764e1ed679025ee5af06a39a95cf53466955/inst/resources/lua/jss.lua#L50-L98

`.t` no more exist and type must be checked using 
```lua
pandoc.utils.type(meta.keywords) == "List"
```

This will work only for Pandoc 2.17 so we need to adjust to use several syntax depending on the Pandoc version probably to not break existing code and not set a hard requirement on Pandoc 2.17

Note that no error is thrown (nothing in CI even following #267) so this will silently have side effect with the Lua filter not applying as it should

title: [chrome_print] automatically stream PDF when Chrome allows it
description:
> Would that mean compatibility issues with previous Chrome version and pagedown if we make it the default ?

The compatibility issue would only be with older versions of Chrome which do not support PDF streaming.

But, for now, I think that we could take benefit of Chrome PDF streaming capabilities like this:

1. Check if the available version of Chrome supports PDF streaming: feasible (=> check the remote protocol and test whether the `transferMode` parameter is available in the `Page.printToPDF` command)
2. If Chrome support PDF streaming, change automatically the value of `transferMode` (and allow users to override this behavior)

IMO, this would lead to a better user experience: `chrome_print()` would automatically exploit the available Chrome features. If a user is stuck with a large PDF file, he would only have to upgrade Chrome.

_Originally posted by @RLesur in https://github.com/rstudio/pagedown/issues/205#issuecomment-762171649_

title: Chromium timeout: "ReferenceError: $ is not defined"
description:
Our Shiny app renders pagedown reports, and we've recently started having some reports fail with a Chromium timeout. It seems to be dependent on the report parameters: if I request ten reports, the same 4 or 5 will fail every time, even if I run them again separately, while others will render fine.

Increasing the `timeout` for `chrome_print` often solves this issue, but I had to jack it up to about 5 minutes in one case in order to get one particularly stubborn report to render.

Our Shiny app runs inside a Docker container, and this issue hadn't appeared until recently. But when it did, it not only occured in a new version that we built, but also _old_ versions that had previously worked—if we rebuilt their images. For example, if I pull a previously built image of version 1.1.0 of our Shiny app, our packages run fine, but if I checkout the version of our code at 1.1.0 and rebuild the image locally, reports start failing.

This leads me to conclude that I have an uncontrolled dependency. On the Docker side, the base rocker image and all the R packages are controlled (either through rocker's checkpointing or through devtools), and I've ruled out Chromium (the same version exists both in working versions and failing ones).

When running packages with `verbose = TRUE`, I get one line in the dumps of the failing packages that stands out:

```json
`Message received from headless Chrome: {"method":"Runtime.exceptionThrown","params":{"timestamp":1596519152085.71,"exceptionDetails":{"exceptionId":1,"text":"Uncaught","lineNumber":28389,"columnNumber":8,"url":"http://127.0.0.1:6156/13-Days%20under%2012-085072-Sale-factsheet.html","stackTrace":{"callFrames":[{"functionName":"","scriptId":"47","url":"http://127.0.0.1:6156/13-Days%20under%2012-085072-Sale-factsheet.html","lineNumber":28389,"columnNumber":8}]},"exception":{"type":"object","subtype":"error","className":"ReferenceError","description":"ReferenceError: $ is not defined\n at http://127.0.0.1:6156/13-Days%20under%2012-085072-Sale-factsheet.html:28390:9","objectId":"{\"injectedScriptId\":2,\"id\":1}","preview":{"type":"object","subtype":"error","description":"ReferenceError: $ is not defined\n at http://127.0.0.1:6156/13-Days%20under%2012-085072-Sale-factsheet.html:28390:9","overflow":false,"properties":[{"name":"stack","type":"string","value":"ReferenceError: $ is not defined\n at http://127\u2026s%20under%2012-085072-Sale-factsheet.html:28390:9"},{"name":"message","type":"string","value":"$ is not defined"}]}},"executionContextId":2}}}`
```

The error `ReferenceError: $ is not defined` sounds a lot like a jQuery problem to me. I know that paged.js uses jQuery under the hood, and I don't know how paged.js is packaged with `pagedown`, but I'm wondering if it and its dependencies just sit in the browser cache once I've built my Docker image—or maybe even once I've run reports with the image once (although the fact that I deleted a local image, pulled a previously built one from GitLab and was able to use it makes me think this is being baked in at Docker build time).

Has anyone seen any recent problems with jQuery not always being loaded properly? Thanks!

title: Add support for Edge with Chromium in find_chrome
description:
As discussed with @RLesur, New Edge browser is [[officially out](https://support.microsoft.com/fr-fr/help/4501095/download-the-new-microsoft-edge-based-on-chromium) and it is based on Chromium now, offering the Chrome Devtools Protocol - same one as in Chrome or Chromium headless. 

Here are some ressources on this new version: 

* [Edge Devtools on Chromium](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/devtools-guide-chromium)
* [Edge Devtools Protocol same as Chrome Devtools protocol](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/devtools-protocol-chromium)
* [puppeteer can be used](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/puppeteer) 

I tested that it works with `crrri`, our R 📦 for interfacing with chrome devtools protocol in browser. 

Then I tested with `pagedown::chrome_print` and it works perfectly find just by changing the binary

```r
Sys.setenv(PAGEDOWN_CHROME = "C:/Program Files (x86)/Microsoft/Edge/Application/msedge.exe")
pagedown::chrome_print("https://pagedown.rbind.io/", output = "pagedown.pdf")
```

First good news: `pagedown::chrome_print` works find with new Edge ! 🎉 

For all those who can't have access to chrome or chromium on their computer, but have Edge in the newer version, it could be nice to support Edge browser in find_chrome or at least mention in the doc it works with Edge Chromium. 

The logic could be: 
* Find chrome on windows
* If not found find Edge and check the version to see if it supports chromium

🤷‍♂  Or there could be a `pagedown::edge_print` with a `find_edge` ? 😉 😄

I think this happen because R can't reach chrome even after 15 try spaced by 0.2 sec.

* Increase the default (30 tries instead of 15 or 0.5 sec sleep instead of 0.2)

title: Overruling at-page statement using default-page.css
description:
Paged.js takes into account only the first `@page {...}` statement it finds.  

So, if the user wants to overrule the `@page` statement using a `custom.css` file, it is:
- possible with `html_paged(css = c('custom.css', 'default-page')`
- impossible with `html_paged(css = c('default-page', 'custom.css')`

This is a low priority bug but I'm unsatisfied by this behavior that violates the CSS precedence property.

I see two ways to modify this behavior:
- isolate the `@page` statement in a specific CSS file that could be removed by the user.
- include the `@page` statement in the pandoc template and create variables for paper size and margins (maybe the same as in the pandoc's default LaTeX template).

We also can wait for the bugfix in Paged.js.

title: Native chrome automation for PDF creation
description:
I want to share an experiment I made with @MilesMcBain's [chradle](https://github.com/MilesMcBain/chradle) test package.
The goal of chradle is to communicate with Chrome through the [Devtools Protocol](https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/) (like puppeteer) using a websocket connection (with [rstudio/websocket](https://github.com/rstudio/websocket)): we have a direct connection between R and Chrome.
I only succeeded with a screenshot.
``` r
# remotes::install_github('milesmcbain/chradle')
library(chradle)

session <- chr_init(url = "https://pagedown.rbind.io/", incomming_debug = TRUE)
resp <- chr_call(session, '{"id":3,"method":"Page.captureScreenshot"}')
img <- jsonlite::base64_dec(resp$result$data)
writeBin(img, 'screenshot.png')
# I didn't succeed with a PDF 
# https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/1-3/Page#method-printToPDF
# state <- chr_call(session, '{"id":4,"method":"Page.printToPDF"}')
chr_kill(session)
chr_clean()
```
I found this test extremely interesting: it shows that a Chrome automation for PDF generation (or other tasks) should be feasible from R but it seems to be a huge task (or a side project).
I think we are in a too early stage to work on this... but maybe in the future.
